# Free-model choice after the M1 scope correction

**Decision:** use `openrouter/nex-agi/nex-n2.5-pro:free` as the campaign's selected default when the pending M1 code is released. Configure no automatic model fallback. Preserve users' explicit BYOK choices. This is a model-selection decision, not a claim that the new default is already deployed or that a full live research run succeeded.

**Public evidence (22 September 2026):** [OpenRouter's model page](https://openrouter.ai/nex-agi/nex-n2.5-pro%3Afree) lists this exact route as free, with a 262,144-token context and support for tools and structured outputs. The [public catalog snapshot](nex-pro-public-catalog197.json) records zero prompt and completion prices and the advertised request parameters. Public metadata establishes current eligibility and advertised capabilities, not dependable capacity or scientific quality. The existing request boundary must continue to check prices at call time and impose zero-price ceilings; unknown or newly paid routes fail closed.

**Local evidence already collected:** Nex Pro passed the retained three-trial [current scientific panel](model-qualification/pro-challenge163-summary.json), [usefulness](model-qualification/usefulness-series113-acceptance.json), [ranking](model-qualification/ranking-series114-acceptance.json), and [batch-schema](model-qualification/batch-context120-acceptance.json) checks. This evidence is more relevant to the current workflow than OpenRouter popularity rankings. The account's local campaign run reached interview, public retrieval, verification and ranking, but was paused before report publication at the user's direction. Its slow/error-prone provider calls limit any claim of end-to-end reliability. See [run handoff](local-run-guardian196.json) and the cycle 196–197 plan log.

**Alternatives:** Nex Mini, Dots Preview and Liquid failed their declared scientific gates in the [qualification inventory](model-qualification/README.md). Gemma 26B, Qwen and Nemotron remain *unqualified*, chiefly because of provider errors or incomplete panels; none is labeled scientifically rejected. `openrouter/free` dynamically picks a model, so it would not preserve the selected-model identity or the fixed comparisons used here. No further model benchmarking is authorized for this M1 decision. A fallback can be added in a future scoped change only with evidence of free eligibility and compatibility; it is not required to ship a safe single-model chain.

**Release boundary:** The current app defaults still name MiniMax M3, and the M1 campaign changes are not yet merged or deployed. The M2 release item now owns switching the configured default to the selected route, checking the actual serving configuration, and deploying the accumulated zero-cost safeguards. Until that release is verified, this document is a decision record, not production acceptance.

**23 September availability update:** A fresh [official catalog receipt](nex-pro-catalog-2026-09-23.json) still lists zero prompt/completion prices and now gives an `expiration_date` of **25 September 2026**; the [model page](https://openrouter.ai/nex-agi/nex-n2.5-pro:free) says the free route is going away that day. Nex Pro remains the only candidate that passed the retained full scientific panels. Keep the selected single-model route for the immediate release, with current-price admission and no automatic fallback. Its retirement is a hard stop for later live campaign calls, not a reason to silently route to an unqualified or paid model. Before any post-retirement inference, choose and verify an exact currently free replacement using official catalog information and the retained evidence under the campaign's zero-spend boundary. Static repository assessment can continue while that route is unavailable; this update does not restart M1 model benchmarking.
